title: Arm CEO extends contract to 2033 amid reports Nvidia had approached him for vacant CEO role
html:
Arm CEO Rene Haas has signed an agreement with the chip company to remain in his role until 2033, affirming his “long-term commitment to leading the company through its next phase of growth.”

The company also announced that effective December 1, 2026, Haas will assume the role of vice chairman of SoftBank Group.

SoftBank acquired Arm in 2016 for $32 billion and currently owns almost 90 percent of the chip company. Haas joined Arm in 2013 and has held the role of CEO since 2022.

“I’ve never been more confident about Arm’s future,” said Haas in a statement. “I believe deeply in our people, our strategy and the opportunity ahead. I’m incredibly proud of what we’re building and wholly committed to realizing Arm’s full potential for many years to come.”

The announcement follows reports that Nvidia’s board had approached Haas about its vacant CEO position following former chief executive Jensen Huang’s resignation on November 12.

Huang was ousted from the company after admitting to an affair with a woman accused of spying for the Chinese government. Following this admission, and reports that he had engaged in a second affair with a direct report at Nvidia, Jensen Huang resigned from the chip giant after 33 years leading the company. Reports of a third affair have also surfaced.

Former CFO Colette Kress had been serving as interim CEO for the beleaguered company, but Huang has now been reinstated.

Nvidia VP Ian Buck; AMD CEO Lisa Su; and Apple’s chief hardware officer, Johny Srouji, had been thought to have been approached about the position.
summary: Haas will also assume role of vice chairman at SoftBank on December 1
